assumptions: 2000 random 16-byte keys (seeded); all 128 input bits flipped
bias = |P(output bit flips) - 1/2|; with 2000 keys the sampling standard deviation per cell is about 0.011, so BLAKE2b's values estimate the noise floor
meta.falsification: H-C18-1: a difference > 0.01 in mean or maximal bias. H-C18-2: a structured quasigroup with maximal bias <= that of QG-LS p2+rev. H-C18-3a: NIMINV mean bias above FNV-1a's. H-C18-5: a forward-only variant with maximal bias < 0.5.
meta.hypothesis: H-C18-1 (bold): QG-LS with 2 passes and a reverse pass has mean and maximal avalanche bias within 0.01 of BLAKE2b-64. H-C18-2: every structured quasigroup (AFF, XOR, ARP, ALP) is worse than the random Latin square on maximal avalanche bias. H-C18-3a (bold): the nimber inversion quasigroup (NIMINV, 2 passes + reverse) has avalanche at least as good as FNV-1a-64. H-C18-5 (from Theorem 2): every forward-only variant has maximal bias 0.5.
meta.methodology: For each hash and input bit, flip the bit in all keys and record which output bits change; report mean flip rate, mean and maximal bias, cells with bias > 0.1, deterministic cells, and the maximal/mean absolute correlation between output-bit changes (bit independence).
meta.question: How close to an ideal 64-bit mixer are e-transformation hashes over the seven quasigroups, with 1, 2 or 4 passes and with or without a reverse pass?
meta.title: Strict avalanche and bit independence: 13 quasigroup hash variants against FNV-1a, MX64, BLAKE2b and CRC32
